claims.text: Lignin's heterogeneity, poor solubility and limited reactivity hinder its use as a polyol in polyurethane foams.
You have published EEM fluorescence and DUV Raman analysis of lignin-emissive domains at fibre-cement interfaces.
Your proposal aims to relate lignin type and hydroxyl content to foaming dynamics and cell structure.

Lignin-rich flexible polyurethane foams for
upholstery (proposal, declined)
Summary
We propose to replace up to 30 % of the petroleum polyol in flexible polyurethane foams with kraft
and organosolv lignin. Preliminary foams with 15 % lignin reached a compression set below 10 %.
Aims
1. Formulate flexible foams with 30 % bio-content using fractionated lignin.
2. Relate lignin type and hydroxyl content to foaming dynamics and cell structure.
3. Demonstrate durability under cyclic compression for upholstery use.

Methods
Lignin fractions are characterised by 31P NMR and GPC. Foams are produced in free-rise
conditions and analysed by SEM, compression testing and dynamic mechanical analysis.
Expected outcomes
A formulation window for lignin-rich flexible foams and a dataset linking lignin structure to foam
properties.

Panel summary and reviewer comments
Reviewer 1: The preliminary data are convincing and the team has the right expertise in lignin
chemistry.
Reviewer 2: The applicants do not demonstrate that the foams meet fire-safety standard EN 13501
at the proposed bio-content.
Reviewer 3
Relate lignin type and hydroxyl content to foaming dynamics and cell structure.
